prompt.text:
Implement an arithmetic expression parser in `Solution.java`. Expose `public static Expr parsePrefix(String input)` and `public static Expr parseInfix(String input)`. Define public interface `Expr` and immutable implementations whose `toString()` produces canonical forms: integer literals as ordinary decimal text, `ADD(left,right)`, `MUL(left,right)`, and `NEG(value)`. Prefix grammar is `integer`, `add(expr,expr)`, `mul(expr,expr)`, or `neg(expr)`. Infix grammar supports signed integer literals, binary `+`, binary `*`, unary `-`, and parentheses; unary minus has highest precedence, then multiplication, then addition, with binary operations left-associative. Whitespace may appear anywhere. Null, empty, malformed, overflowing integer literals, trailing input, and missing operands must throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Parsing must retain no mutable alias to the input.
